_help: The machine half of docs/RULEBOOK.md: what pipeline/playbook_check.py enforces on every hook, spoken line, static's words and ad copy line, and the targets the weekly review measures against. EDIT THIS FILE after a weekly performance review (or run `python3 pipeline/weekly_review.py add ...`): a new banned phrase, a phrase that won, a changed target. Every rule has `why` (who said it, when, the evidence) and `level`: `hard` stops `ideas.py check` / `plan` (exit 2), `soft` is a warning in the plan output and the run report. Patterns are case-insensitive Python regexes matched on whole words. Keep the change log at the bottom: one line per meeting.

kpi._help: Targets the weekly review (weekly_review.py report) compares every ad against. Hook rate = 3-second video plays / impressions; hold rate = ThruPlays / 3-second plays; Meta's own columns.

hook_rate.why: Julian 2026-11-05: 'hook rate would be amazing if it's like 45%. 40 to 45 to 50% even would be crazy good'; = 3-s plays / impressions

hold_rate.why: Julian 2026-11-05: 'hold rate is good if it's around 10, 15%' = ThruPlays / impressions ('of 1,000 people ... 12% watched the entire ad')

ctr.why: the creator winners run 4.7-10.5% CTR (docs/research/2026-11-all-time-best-ad.md section 1)

roas.why: Julian 2026-11-05: 'ROAS would be ideal 2.1 or above'; 2.5 = 'really performing well, we can increase budgets'

cpa.why: Julian 2026-11-05: 'cost per result should be around 30 max' (the ad account reports in AUD)

cpm.note: Not a creative KPI (Julian 2026-11-05): Q4 / Black Friday lifts it, Vintage runs ~90-100 AUD vs Hobo ~46-78; only a very high CPM hints that Meta dislikes a claim

batch.why: Julian 2026-11-05: 'better to have very good 12 ads instead of 25 or 27 that are average ... volume is good only if we can have quality': a batch with no numbers makes 12 statics (+ 5 projects)

hooks._help: Every hook: the 4 spoken openings of a project (ideas.json hooks[].text), the first line of a static's words, primary text 1's first line in ad_copy.csv.

must_be_concrete.why: A hook that names nothing the viewer can SEE (keys, a zip, a train, a crowd: shotmatch.py's footage words) or a number AND follows none of the formulas below is hard (hook_generic): a statement nobody stops for. Concrete but formula-less, or a formula with nothing to see, is a warning. Halbert: a headline flags its reader with self-interest; our feature-list losers opened on vague lines.

opener_reuse.why: B030-B034 opened 5 projects with 'Black Friday prices are live now, and ...': Meta groups ads with the same look and story as one (Meta, Dec 2025). The first 4 words of a hook may not repeat a hook of the product's last 8 batches or another hook of this sheet.

third_person.why: The viewer is 'you'. 'Her keys are at the bottom of the bag again' (B032 P02 H3) speaks about a stranger; only a gift / friend structure talks about 'her'.

formula_needed.why: Each hook should follow one of the proven formulas below (Halbert's 349 headlines + our winners); a hook that matches none is usually a statement nobody stops for.

formulas.name: How to ...
formulas.example: How to carry your cards through a crowd without checking your bag.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'How To Make A Fortune Today Starting From Scratch'

formulas.name: A question only the target answers yes to
formulas.example: Still digging for your keys at the front door?
formulas.source: Halbert: 'Are You Ever Tongue-Tied At A Party?'; winners 158-H2, C9_V2

formulas.name: A number of specific things
formulas.example: Three things this bag does that yours doesn't.
formulas.source: Halbert: '7 Ways To Collect Your Unpaid Bills'; winners MAX-33-H5 ('3 reasons'), 139-H4 ('4 reasons')

formulas.name: Do you make these mistakes / the costly mistake
formulas.example: The mistake that leaves your phone at the bottom of your bag.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'The 5 Most Costly Mistakes In Business - How Many Are You Making?'

formulas.name: Before you buy / a warning
formulas.rx: ^(?:before you|don't buy|do not buy|warning|careful)\b|\bbefore you buy\b
formulas.example: Before you buy another handbag, look at its back.
formulas.source: winner 158-H2 ('Before you buy one of my bags, I need to warn you'); Halbert: 'Using A Lawyer May Be Dangerous To Your Wealth'

formulas.name: Ordinary vs this / then vs now
formulas.example: Most bags hang open in a crowd. Watch this one.
formulas.source: our only AI winner B017 P04 'ordinary bag vs the Hobo 2.0' (ROAS 2.97); Halbert: 'Don't Try This With Any Other Copier'

formulas.name: A command to watch a demo
formulas.example: Watch what one pull of this zip does.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'Throw Away Your Oars!'; the proof shot of every story video

formulas.name: A specific moment (time, place)
formulas.example: Packed train, both hands on the rail. Where's your phone?
formulas.source: Halbert: 'Suppose This Happened On Your Wedding Day!'; story statics 2026-11-04

formulas.name: At last / finally / new
formulas.example: At last, a soft bag that zips all the way shut.

formulas.name: The truth / what nobody tells you
formulas.rx: \b(?:truth about|nobody tells you|what everybody ought to know|the real reason|here's why|the reason)\b
formulas.example: The truth about big bags: they swallow your phone.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'The Truth About Getting Rich', 'What Everybody Ought To Know About ...'

formulas.name: Imagine / what if
formulas.example: What if your keys had their own place in your bag?
formulas.source: Halbert: 'Imagine Working Until 4:00 A.M. - And Loving Every Minute Of It!'

formulas.name: If you can X, you can Y / if you X
formulas.example: If you can snap a clasp, you can close this bag one-handed.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'If You Can Lick A Stamp - You Can Lick Your Weight Problem'

formulas.name: Who else / for the woman who
formulas.example: For the woman who changes bags before every plan.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'For The Woman Who Is Older Than She Looks', 'To Men Who Want To Quit Work Someday'

formulas.name: The hidden / the one place
formulas.example: The pocket nobody behind you can reach.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'Profits That Lie Hidden In Your Farm' (only a literal hidden feature: never 'the secret to')

formulas.name: The offer as news (one hook a project at most)
formulas.rx: \b(?:\d+ ?%|percent|half price|black friday|cyber monday|for the price of)\b
formulas.example: Three bags for the price of one this Black Friday.
formulas.source: Halbert: 'Take Any 3 Of These Kitchen Appliances - For Only $8.95'; ideas.check allows one price hook a project

attention_words._help: From Halbert's 152 Attention Grabber Words, the ones that fit a handbag brand and Meta's rules. Use them; they are not required.

banned._help: Phrases that may not appear in any hook, spoken line, static's words or ad copy line we write (the client's RAW audio and verbatim reviews are exempt: compliance.py checks those). level hard = stops the plan.

rules.rx: black friday prices are live(?: now)?
rules.why: the owner's own line (campaign.json client_ideas), but B030-B034 opened 14 hooks with it: Meta reads one template as one ad. Allowed, a warning; opener_reuse (hard) refuses it once the last 8 batches have it
a name-the-product opener: no reader is flagged, nothing happens (Halbert: the headline must flag the reader with self-interest)
a line that only names the bag (the team 2026-11-04: 'The everyday hobo.' is not a story)

rules.rx: \b(?:game[- ]?changer|must[- ]have|obsessed|holy grail|life[- ]?changing|you won't believe|you need this|look no further|elevate your|level up|next level|insane|viral|tiktok made me)\b
rules.why: influencer filler: says nothing the picture can show; reads as AI copy
Halbert's hype words date the copy and Meta's ranking reads them as low quality; show the thing instead

rules.rx: \b(?:everyone(?:'s| is) (?:talking|buying|obsessed)|everyone won't stop|thousands of (?:women|customers|people)|\d[\d,]* (?:women|customers|people|orders|happy)|best[- ]?sell\w*|#1|number one bag|most popular|the bag everyone)\b
rules.why: invented social proof (PLAYBOOK section 9: no invented numbers or claims)

rules.rx: \b(?:selling (?:out|fast)|sold out|almost gone|only \d+ left|low stock|limited stock|while (?:they|it|stocks?) lasts?|final hours|hurry|don't miss out|before it's gone|before they're gone|going fast)\b
rules.why: no stock claim or countdown nobody confirmed (CLAUDE.md section S). The dated campaign words ('last chance' from 20 Nov, 'ends tonight' on 30 Nov) are judged by campaign.json's own rules
an absolute the facts don't back ('anti-theft' and 'lockable' are fine; 'theft-proof' never)
the facts say water-resistant
the same % runs all year (site banner): unprovable (PLAYBOOK section 5)
the brand voice and the presenter talk in 'you' form, never as a customer (CLAUDE.md rule 1, PLAYBOOK section 9)
a static never fakes a button; the CTA is Meta's button ('Tap the link below.' is only the video's last line)
Julian 2026-11-05: we target the US, UK and Australia broad; UK ships free too: say 'free shipping'

claims._help: Property words a line may use only when the product's facts (compliance.context corpus: the site, PLAYBOOK section 1, the product file) say them. `fact` = the words that must be in the facts (default: the matched words). compliance.py already covers waterproof, leather grades, best-seller, star ratings, theft-proof.

rules.why: only the Hobo 2.0 has an RFID lining
only a bag with lockable zippers may say it locks
only the Hobo 2.0 strap is cut-resistant
no product fact gives the weight
no product fact says what device fits; name what the facts list (phone, wallet, keys)

rules.rx: holds? everything|fits everything|room for everything|everything you (?:own|need)
rules.why: an absolute; say what fits
no material claim the facts don't make
the facts say 'leather' / 'leather-look' only (research 2026-11: the word leather needs the owner)
never handmade unless the facts say so (the RAW story is the client's own)

rules.rx: lasts? (?:for )?(?:years|a lifetime|forever)|lifetime (?:bag|quality|warranty)|built to last|never wears? out|indestructible
rules.why: the facts give a 1-year warranty, no lifetime
the warranty is 1 year (C9_V2's RAW said two)
Black Friday items are final sale; only when the facts say it

copy._help: ad_copy.csv limits (Meta). The checker also runs the banned rules and the hook rules on primary text 1's first line.

em_dash.why: Wouter / PLAYBOOK section 10: no em dashes (reads as AI copy)

footage._help: The b-roll must show what the line says (Julian 2026-10-21; owner 2026-11-05: 'it should not happen'). shotmatch.py scores the moment a shot plays against the words said over it.
footage.why: plan (ideas.check): a chapter whose `show` tag has fewer good footage moments than min_moments_for_show_tag for the product is refused (low_coverage_level). Render (storyboard.plan_block): a shot under words that name a feature (shotmatch.SPECIFIC) that shows none of them is swapped for a later pick or a spare that does. After render (make_batch.footage_match): any shot still showing none of what is said is 'shot mismatch' (mismatch_level hard: upload skips that version; qa/<id>_footage.json lists each shot).

presenter._help: How many projects of a batch carry the presenter (owner 2026-11-05: 'the presenter UGC videos are good, we need to make more of that'). Key = projects in the batch (the highest key not above it applies). The request's own number or 'no presenter' always wins.
presenter.why: ~225 credits a presenter project; 3 of 5 is ~700, inside presenter.CAP (1000)
notes: Julian 2026-11-05 on B028 P02 (Vintage, the presenter): 'I like the metrics ... it's just the hook is not really strong' (hook rate 32-33%): make new hooks for it
no label over her hook: she says it and the caption shows it ('keep either this one or this one, not both, the smaller one is cleaner')
do not open her video with Black Friday ('a UGC video has to look less aggressive'): the moment first, the sale at the end
no dead pauses ('this pause is a bit useless ... it loses momentum'): presenter.py gate flags a pause over 0.6 s, fails one over 1.0 s
a line that names something to see cuts to that footage while it is said ('one hand holds the coffee, but the clip of the coffee comes later')
b-roll in talking-head videos may run longer; b-roll-only videos 3-5 s max a clip

art: The bag big and in the centre; no empty space ('empty space on statics is always bad'), but not crowded
The offer once and big: never again in the headline ('too many times 60% off')
A catchy benefit headline, never a feature name ('hidden pocket doesn't say much'; 'Looks expensive, works three ways' is better)
Post-it / note statics: make the note look real (not AI) and the text aggressive, not a list of features
No review card on story statics (only the quote look); Trustpilot reviews later if the site gets them back
Us vs them: show THEM too, an ordinary tote, grey / a bit green / low quality; ours in warm, rich colour (brand_statics.them_half)
Words never over the bag or its strap; a shop-window decal sits ON the glass with the bag behind it; nothing tilted by accident
Show the bag, not only the free pouch: people buy the bag, the pouch is the extra
3-Piece Set: 60% off (as on the site), never 50%
'Which colour are you?' / pick-your-colour catalog statics win: make one for every bag with 4+ colours (Vintage next)

keep_winners.why: a batch of 6+ statics carries the proven winners' layouts (pick your colour ROAS 2.93; set value 2.57) next to the new formats

winning_patterns._help: What the account's money says works (docs/research/2026-11-all-time-best-ad.md, the weekly reviews). The strategy packet prints these; weekly_review.py adds to them.

items.rule: Contrast beats lists: an ordinary bag vs this one, shown side by side.
items.evidence: B017 P04 versus ROAS 2.97 ($256); B017 statics 'Yes, the zip locks.' 2.91

items.rule: One idea per video, shown not told; at most 3 features.
items.evidence: the engine's 'n things' / 'stop' feature lists: ROAS 1.69-2.21

items.rule: The first sentence opens a loop the body closes (a warning, a question, a doubt said out loud).
items.evidence: creator winners 158-H2, 139-H4, C9_V2: CTR 4.7-9%

items.rule: 3-5 numbered reasons, each a feature the hands show.
items.evidence: MAX-33-H5 (3 reasons) ROAS 2.85; 94-H4 (5 reasons) 3.84

items.rule: Say the doubt out loud, then answer it ('a secure bag doesn't have to look tactical').
items.evidence: the creator winners' transcripts

items.rule: A person on camera beats a faceless voiceover: the presenter project of every batch, the bag worn in 2+ chapters.
items.evidence: creator winners CPA $22-31; owner 2026-11-05 'the presenter UGC videos are good'

items.rule: The 3-Piece Set lifts order value.
items.evidence: DEC08 set ads ROAS 2.85-3.34, orders $92-109

items.rule: Pick-your-colour catalog static ('Which colour are you?'): every colour of the bag, catalog style
items.evidence: S09_pick_your_colour (our first batch, Oct): 2,285 AUD, ROAS 2.93, 76 purchases, CPA 30 AUD: our best ad; Julian 2026-11-05: 'this one has been doing really, really good'

items.rule: A real footage frame + one short proof line ('Yes, the zip locks.')
items.evidence: B017 S04 native: 798 AUD, ROAS 2.46, 21 purchases (Oct 6 - Nov 4), our best ad

items.rule: Question hooks about a moment ('Where does everything go when you pack a weekend bag?')
items.evidence: Oct 6 - Nov 4: question hooks 52% hook rate, ROAS 2.45 vs offer hooks 43%, 1.39

items.rule: Anti-theft in crowds: trains, the metro, travel, busy tourist spots (Hobo 2.0 and Hobo Bag, statics and videos)
items.evidence: Julian 2026-11-05: 'this is a good angle ... we should use this also in video ads'

items.rule: The gifting angle for Christmas and Black Friday
items.evidence: Julian 2026-11-05: 'I like gifting angle for Christmas. It's really good.'

items.rule: Statics drive the results now (and Google Ads needs statics): quality over volume
items.evidence: Oct 6 - Nov 4: our statics ROAS 2.18 vs videos 1.45; Julian: 'the main performance are statics'

items.rule: The 3-Piece Set value static (the three pieces, the set price / 60% off, 'Best Value')
items.evidence: S07_set3_value: 2,638 AUD, ROAS 2.57, 70 purchases; S06_set3_card3 ROAS 4.17 (Oct 6 - Nov 4)

items.rule: Simple, real-photo brand statics (colours, value, bold offer, meet-the-bag) outsell the AI-designed formats so far: every batch keeps one or two of the proven layouts next to the new formats
items.evidence: Oct 6 - Nov 4: our first batches (real-photo layouts) 8,162 AUD at ROAS 2.57 (234 purchases) vs B016-B029 (AI concepts / ads) 4,952 AUD at 1.67; the account's other ads 2.06. (The early ads had longer to run.)

items.rule: Five features in 7-8 chapters under a different frame.
items.evidence: B025 / B027 (PLAYBOOK 4k)

items.rule: Hooks that open on the discount (more than one a project).
items.evidence: B025 / B027; one price hook a project since 2026-10-27

items.rule: Opening on the bag just sitting there (hero / placed).
items.evidence: B025 / B027 most used shot tags

items.rule: One hook template across batches ('Black Friday prices are live now, and ...').
Hooks that open on the sale ('Black Friday prices are live now', 'Fifty percent off ...')
items.evidence: Oct 6 - Nov 4: 7 offer hooks spent 1,646 AUD at ROAS 1.39; B016 P02 H4 0.32; B028 P02 H4 33% hook rate

items.rule: B-roll that arrives after the words ('the coffee clip comes later'), or shows something else (crossbody line over another clip)
items.evidence: Julian 2026-11-05 on B028 and V09

items.rule: Static headlines that only name a feature ('The hidden back pocket.', 'Lockable zippers.')
Footage stills that show the pouch more than the bag
items.evidence: Julian 2026-11-05: 'I would not launch this one'

process.review_call: Weekly call with Julian, same time every week, 15:00 Italy time (19:30 IST): bring the ads that got spend; he gives feedback only on those
process.pre_launch: Both sides look at a batch before launch (tracker Status 🔍 Review -> ✅ Ready)
process.testing: Julian tests in CBO now (Meta spreads the budget); ABO ad sets that overspent were killed

changelog.change: rulebook created: hook formulas from Halbert's 349 headlines, banned phrases from B001-B038, hook rate target 40-45%, footage match blocker, presenter in about half the projects
KPIs: hook rate 40-50%, hold rate (ThruPlays / impressions) 10-15%, ROAS 2.1 (scale at 2.5), CPA 30 AUD max; CPM is not a creative KPI
presenter: no hook label, no sale in her hooks, pauses over 1 s fail the take, footage cuts in on the words that name it
statics: 12 a batch by default (quality over volume), the offer once, benefit headlines, no review card on story statics, us-vs-them shows them grey, the bag big
copy: 'free shipping', never 'free US shipping' (UK ships free too)
first numbers (Oct 6 - Nov 4): question hooks 52% vs offer hooks 43%; statics ROAS 2.18 vs videos 1.45; best ad B017 S04 'Yes, the zip locks.' ROAS 2.46

our first batches' real-photo statics are the account's best: S09_pick_your_colour ROAS 2.93 (76 purchases), S07_set3_value 2.57 (70); a batch of 6+ statics keeps a colours and a value static.
